WHAT_THIS_CORRECTS: Two turns ago I recorded that a persistent resident 'needs an ownership record the next pool can adopt rather than reap' and that this is 'a lifetime/ownership feature with its own failure mode, not a patch'. That was wrong in an important way: the ownership record, the claim-based sparing, the intentional-detachment flag and the start-token are ALL already implemented. I diagnosed a missing feature by reading only the path I happened to be driving.
THIRD_TIME_THIS_SESSION: The same error shape as the drive_resident scorer, the missing cost function, and the missing rejection feedback: concluding a capability is absent after exercising one route to it. My own standing rule -- grep for CALL SITES, and check for a sibling that already does it -- would have caught this earlier.
WHAT_G023_ACTUALLY_NEEDS_NOW: Verify empirically that the daemon path reuses a loaded resident across rounds (round-2 complete_payload < 60 s, the pre-committed kill).

Put the verified decide() in FRONT of that reuse so a stale, wrong-model, wrong-config or unhealthy daemon is refused rather than blindly reused -- the daemon path spares by CLAIM alone, which is exactly the 'never adopt on a bare PID' failure S010 forbids.
Confirm no double resident and SIGKILL recovery on the daemon path.
THE_ADOPTION_CORE_IS_STILL_THE_RIGHT_WOR: is_orphaned() spares any body whose pid appears in state.json. It does not check model hash, config hash, readiness, responsiveness, heartbeat age or footprint. That is adoption on a bare PID, which is the specific thing S010 3 forbids, so the 17-control decide() belongs in front of it rather than replacing it.
